claim_being_audited: That certifying the model is compliant and evidentially supported on the current record because aggregate readiness passed, no severity-one rehearsal incidents occurred, and the remaining clinical-trial intake weakness can be handled through documented caveats and ongoing monitoring.
decision_criteria: If admissible evidence shows the limitation was explicitly disclosed in the certification/model-card record before launch, the case could move toward compliant_with_caveats.
If admissible evidence shows approved risk acceptance or an approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion, the certification case becomes materially stronger.
If neither disclosure nor approved risk acceptance/mitigation exists, certifying the model remains unsupported and would move toward noncompliant.
Aggregate readiness pass and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents are supportive but not sufficient to override the unresolved disclosure predicate.
evidence_requests: Provide the finalized model card or certification record showing the clinical-trial intake limitation is explicitly disclosed for the named launch use case.
Provide approved risk acceptance, if any, covering the unresolved clinical-trial intake issue before launch.
Provide an approved mitigation/runbook containing owner, alert threshold, review date, and rollback criterion.
Clarify whether the certification decision being audited is unconditional certification now or certification only after the disclosure record is corrected.
specific_concerns: The admissible record shows a named launch-use-case slice remains below target in clinical-trial intake, concentrated in protocol eligibility support.
The current model-card draft says there are no known material limitations even though the record contains a reviewer flag indicating this unresolved issue may need disclosure.
The policy requires material limitations for named launch use cases to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
The proposed mitigation runbook is still draft status and lacks an accountable owner and alert threshold, so it does not satisfy the policy condition for an approved mitigation.
The actor's packet relies in part on public monitoring guidance, but that guidance does not itself satisfy the internal approval and disclosure predicates in the policy text.
unsupported_claims: The recommendation to 'certify_model' is not fully supported on the current record because there is no admissible evidence that the required disclosure has already been made or that approved risk acceptance exists.
The packet's framing that certification is presently 'supportable' depends on a future or implied caveat trail rather than evidence that the caveat trail is already in place.

Public risk-management and model-card guidance support monitoring and documentation generally, but they do not independently establish compliance with the specific internal release-policy requirement.
